system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, no language over the 15-page cell broadcast maximum, the encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

data.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. Encodings are correct: Arabic is UCS-2 and English is GSM-7. Page counts (en 4, ar 7) are within the 15-page cell broadcast maximum. The problem is the first page. In both languages it carries only the dust/sand hazard and no protective action. The only action, 'leave the area now', appears on the last page and belongs to a different, unconfirmed hazard: a dam burst near Al Ain. Moving that line to page 1 would make an evacuation order for an unconfirmed report the lead instruction. A person must decide whether the dam report is real and whether it belongs in this alert or a separate one. Only then can the first page be fixed.

objections.issue: The first page in both languages states the dust/sand hazard but gives no action. The only action in the message ('leave the area now') sits on the final page (page 4 of 4 in English, page 7 of 7 in Arabic), so many readers will not reach it.
objections.fix: Put a protective action for the dust/sand hazard (e.g. reduce driving speed, stay indoors if respiratory-sensitive) in the first sentence, alongside the hazard, in both en and ar.

objections.issue: The message mixes two hazards. A second hazard, a dam burst with an evacuation instruction, is attached at the end of the dust alert and attributed only to 'Reports say'. A person must decide whether it is confirmed and whether it should go out as its own alert, with its hazard and action on page 1. It should not be buried on the last page of a weather alert.
objections.fix: Refer to the approvers. If the dam burst is confirmed, issue a separate alert that leads with the dam hazard and the evacuation action. If it is not confirmed, remove it from this alert.

no_basis.concern: The dam-burst line is attributed only to unnamed reports, not to an official source, and it comes after the stated source (National Centre of Meteorology). Verifying the source is not covered by any network/handset clause I was shown.
